title: Taifa of Seville
capsule: The Taifa of Seville was a Muslim principality in al-Andalus that rose from the fragmentation of the Córdoba Caliphate after 1031, governed by the Abbadid dynasty. Under Abbad II al-Mu'tadid (1042–1069) it aggressively absorbed neighboring taifas, and his son Muhammad al-Mu'tamid (1069–1091) presided over a court that became the premier literary and intellectual center of al-Andalus, hosting the astronomer al-Zarqali and drawing refugee scholars after Toledo's fall to Alfonso VI in 1085. Al-Mu'tamid invited the Almoravids from North Africa to halt Castilian expansion; they halted Alfonso VI at the Battle of Sagrajas (1086) but then turned against their Muslim allies, and in 1091 Almoravid forces occupied Seville, exiling al-Mu'tamid to Morocco where he died in captivity.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Territorial extent is moderately well attested through Arabic chronicles and modern scholarship on al-Andalus, though exact boundaries of the taifa's fluctuating dependencies remain approximate.
